NBC Los Angeles: Jury finds Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk not guilty in murder-for-hire case

Rolling Stone: Lil Durk acquitted of all charges at murder-for-hire trial

content.p: On Friday 11 September 2026 a federal jury in Los Angeles found the rapper Lil Durk, whose legal name is Durk Banks, not guilty on every count he faced in a murder-for-hire trial. He had been accused of paying for an attempt to kill the rival rapper Quando Rondo, a shooting that instead killed Rondo's 24-year-old cousin, Saviay'a Robinson. Jurors took three days to reach their verdict.

The result was split. Two co-defendants, Deandre Wilson and David Lindsey, were found guilty on the stalking side of the indictment, including the count that covers a death, but the jury cleared both of the murder-for-hire charges. Banks did not go free. He stayed in custody because a separate racketeering case, severed from this trial, was still waiting. That case was later put off until August 2027.

Prosecutors said the attack happened in broad daylight on 19 August 2022, at a gas station across from the Beverly Center shopping mall. Rondo, whose legal name is Tyquian Bowman, was in a black Escalade with his cousin. According to NBC Los Angeles, prosecutors said gunmen fired at least 18 rounds at the vehicle. Jurors watched video showing three gunmen, one of them armed with a Glock that was allegedly modified to fire automatically, according to Rolling Stone. Rondo survived. Robinson, known as Lul Pab, was struck several times and killed, according to the charging documents as described by the Chicago Tribune.

At a hearing a year earlier, Robinson's mother, Andrea Robinson, told the court she was devastated by the loss of her only child. "I never in a million years thought I'd lose my baby," she said. She said he had three children.

The government's theory ran back to November 2020, when the rapper King Von, whose legal name was Dayvon Bennett, was shot dead at an Atlanta nightclub. Von was a close friend and protege of Banks and part of Only The Family, the Chicago hip-hop collective Banks founded. Prosecutors alleged that someone from Rondo's entourage fired the fatal shots, and that Banks wanted revenge.

In closing arguments, prosecutors told jurors that Banks "wanted revenge" and made that clear to members of the collective in text messages. They described a man who "had his shooters on speed dial" and allegedly decided "it was time to kill" Rondo while he was visiting Los Angeles. The government examined GPS records, texts, flight purchases charged to Banks's credit card, interviews and lyrics that referred to "sliding for Von", according to Complex.

Banks was arrested in October 2024 near a Florida airport, hours after an indictment against his co-defendants was unsealed, the Tribune reported. Prosecutors alleged he had bought seats on three international flights shortly before his arrest. His lawyers have disputed the government's account of his travel plans, according to The Source. He pleaded not guilty and stayed in federal custody in Los Angeles. Judge Fitzgerald refused bail several times, noting that the possibility of life without parole "could make flight the rational choice for any innocent defendant", according to Revolt.

The indictment changed over time. A second superseding indictment in May 2025 removed language suggesting that Banks's lyrics referred to the 2022 killing, and added a count of stalking resulting in death. Banks's lawyer Jonathan Brayman called the removal a significant vindication. About two months before the trial, prosecutors filed a third superseding indictment adding murder in aid of racketeering and a related firearms count, which alleged that Banks ran a criminal enterprise. Judge Fitzgerald would not let those counts be tried alongside the murder-for-hire case, finding they had been brought too close to the trial date for the defence to prepare, according to Law Commentary. They were severed.

The trial took place in downtown Los Angeles. CNN described it as a two-week trial and Rolling Stone as three weeks. Crowds of fans and content creators gathered outside, and the musicians Machine Gun Kelly and Ye attended. Banks pleaded not guilty to five counts. Three were stalking offences (a conspiracy, one involving a weapon, one resulting in a death) and two accused him of murder for hire. He did not testify, and Rondo was not called as a witness, NBC Los Angeles reported.

The prosecution leaned heavily on three men who had made plea deals. Kasey Hester and Keith Jones, two of the gunmen, told jurors they opened fire expecting to be paid by Banks, and they had pleaded guilty to charges including murder and murder for hire, Rolling Stone reported. The third, Kavon Grant, was Banks's former personal assistant. He described himself as a broker of high-end stolen vehicles, pleaded guilty, and, according to Rolling Stone, was the one who obtained the guns and the stolen Infiniti used in the attack. Grant testified that Banks set the plan in motion after learning Rondo would be in Los Angeles, and that Banks directed him to get a stolen car.

Hester said that on 18 August 2022 a phone call told him to go to the airport for an urgent trip, and that on speakerphone he made out Banks talking on a different call. He also said that earlier in the year Banks had complained that the rapper 6ix9ine was taunting him to "slide for Von", and had told the group that anyone who killed Rondo would "be straight". Jones said Wilson told him on a video call that "Durk got a million for us".

Banks's lawyers called the cooperators admitted killers who implicated him to avoid life sentences. Findling described Grant as a "fraudster" and a "master of deception" who planned the shooting without Banks's knowledge and later steered prosecutors toward him. He pointed out that Banks fired Grant in early 2023, months after the killing. "This case is flooded. It is a tsunami of reasonable doubt," Findling said, calling it "a bounty case with no money".

The defence called Hester's wife, who said the phone call that supposedly sent her husband to California never happened. Prosecutors argued she was upset that he had decided to cooperate. A defence witness who had known King Von testified that Grant had helped manage Von's finances, and called him "a liar and a thief". Brian Steel confronted Hester with a May 2023 jail call in which Hester told his wife, "Whatever it takes to make sure I don't do no time."
content.h2: Lyrics, a video and a podcast clip
content.p: Music was part of the evidence. Jurors saw an unreleased video, "Redman", filmed in January 2021, in which Banks mourns King Von and then chases and shoots an actor whom prosecutors said portrayed Rondo. Prosecutors called it evidence of a motive for revenge. Steel called it the creative work of a "grief-stricken" poet. Findling told jurors that "the get-back is a diss track". The judge also admitted lyrics from several songs.

A dispute arose over a 2023 interview with the podcaster DJ Akademiks. Asked whether he was still triggered by the "slide for Von" comments, Banks said he no longer saw them, adding, "it might be the water." In rebuttal, Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Morse called this "absolutely clear" proof that Banks was admitting involvement in Robinson's killing. After deliberations began the defence asked the judge to reopen the evidence so jurors could see more of the three-hour interview, and cited a livestream in which Akademiks said the segment had been scripted. Fitzgerald refused, saying jurors could just as reasonably see Banks as an outsider commenting on the aftermath.

Deliberations began on Wednesday 9 September. When the verdict came on Friday, Rolling Stone reported that Banks hung his head and cried, and that his wife wrapped her arm around his mother. Findling said outside the court that "Durk is not guilty of all charges" and that "the shackles must come off, and he must walk free." Banks's father said he sympathised with the family of the man who died.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said the jury had delivered justice to Robinson's family by convicting Wilson and Lindsey, and added that prosecutors were disappointed about Banks and would present their evidence at his second trial. Wilson's lawyer, Craig Harbaugh, thanked the jury "for seeing there was no murder for hire" and said he expected the remaining counts to fail on a pending motion for acquittal. The stalking-resulting-in-death count carries a maximum of life in prison, according to Complex.

Banks stayed in custody. The racketeering case, which alleges that an Only The Family group ran as a violent organisation, includes the Rondo shooting along with an alleged 2019 attempted killing in Atlanta and a 2022 killing in Chicago, according to Law Commentary. It had been set for 5 October 2026. On 30 September Judge Fitzgerald moved it to 30 August 2027 after the defendants asked for more time and prosecutors did not object, finding the case complex because of the number of defendants and the volume of evidence.

His lawyers have argued that the acquittal changes the picture because the allegations overlap, and they are expected to seek dismissal of the remaining case. A hearing on his release is set for 4 November. Earlier, his lawyers had called the racketeering charges a "pathetic pivot". The verdict does not resolve the racketeering case, which Rolling Stone said would go before a new jury, and prosecutors have said they will present their evidence at the second trial.
